intro: If you're a portfolio landlord with several properties, you're probably looking for an accountant near you who understands the particular demands of property accounting. You need someone who can produce accounts by property, prepare lender-ready figures and help you plan for the longer term. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant who quotes you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What portfolio landlords typically need from an accountant
need_lead: A portfolio landlord's accounting needs go beyond a single rental property, so the right accountant should be able to handle the detail and the bigger picture.
needs: You have several properties and need clear, separate accounts for each one, so you can see how each is performing.
Your lender has asked for business plans and cash-flow forecasts, and you need these prepared accurately.
You're thinking about future purchases and want to know whether a company structure might suit your plans.
You need to keep capital and revenue spending distinct, so your records are clear and your tax position is correct.
You want an accountant near you who can meet in person or locally, and who understands the local property market.
context_heading: What to understand about finding an accountant near you
context: In the UK, the word 'accountant' on its own is not a protected title, so anyone can use it. Titles such as Chartered Accountant (ICAEW, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland), Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA) and Chartered Management Accountant (CIMA) are protected, and members are bound by their body's ethics, training and complaints rules. Only registered auditors can sign statutory audit reports.

Every practice offering accountancy services must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. It is reasonable to ask which body supervises a firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how complaints are handled.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us how many properties you have and where they are located, so we can introduce you to an accountant near you.
Explain whether your properties are held personally, in a company or in a partnership, as this affects the accounting approach.
Mention if you have a lender asking for business plans or cash-flow forecasts, so the accountant can prepare these.
Let us know if you are considering buying more properties and want advice on whether a company structure might be suitable.
Describe how you currently track capital and revenue spending, and whether you need help keeping these separate.
Tell us if you have a mix of residential and commercial property, as the accounting rules can differ.
questions: How will you produce accounts by property so I can see the performance of each one?
Can you help prepare lender-ready figures, including business plans and cash-flow forecasts?
What is your experience with portfolio landlords and property accounting?
How would you advise me on whether a company structure suits future purchases?
How do you help clients keep capital and revenue spending separate?
Which professional body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?

faqs.q: Why might a portfolio landlord need an accountant near them?
faqs.a: A portfolio landlord with several properties has more complex accounting needs than a single-property landlord. An accountant near you can provide accounts by property, lender-ready figures and help with longer-term structure planning, and may be able to meet in person to discuss your portfolio.

faqs.q: What does 'lender-ready figures' mean for a portfolio landlord?
faqs.a: Lenders may ask for business plans and cash-flow forecasts when assessing a portfolio landlord's borrowing. An accountant can prepare these figures from your property accounts, so you can present a clear financial picture to the lender.

faqs.q: Should I hold my properties in a company?
faqs.a: Whether a company structure suits you depends on your circumstances and future plans. An accountant can discuss the potential advantages and disadvantages, such as tax treatment and administration, and help you decide whether it is right for future purchases.

faqs.q: How can an accountant help with capital and revenue spending?
faqs.a: Keeping capital and revenue spending separate is important for accurate tax reporting and for understanding your portfolio's performance. An accountant can help you set up a system to track these separately and ensure your records are clear.

extra_heading: What to expect at a first meeting about your portfolio
extra: A first meeting with an accountant about a property portfolio is usually a working session rather than a sales pitch. Expect to talk through each property in turn, how it is held and what records you already keep, so the accountant can see where the gaps are. It helps to bring a simple list of your properties and any lender correspondence you have received.

Much of the conversation tends to centre on the questions that matter for a portfolio rather than a single letting: how accounts by property will be presented, how capital and revenue spending will be separated, and whether a company structure could suit purchases you are considering. If a lender has asked for business plans or cash-flow forecasts, say so early, because those figures are usually built from the same records as your accounts.

Because fees are quoted on application, ask how the accountant would charge for portfolio work and what that covers, so you can compare like with like. It is also fair to ask who in the practice would look after your affairs day to day, and how they prefer to receive information from you.

extra_faqs.q: Is an accountant near me better than one further away for a property portfolio?
extra_faqs.a: Proximity can help if you prefer to hand over paperwork or sit down in person, but the deciding factor should be whether the accountant regularly deals with portfolios like yours. Ask how they would produce accounts by property and handle lender requests, then weigh that against the convenience of a local meeting.

extra_faqs.q: How do I compare accountants for a portfolio when fees are on application?
extra_faqs.a: Ask each one to set out what the fee covers, such as accounts by property, lender-ready figures or advice on structure, so you can compare the same scope rather than headline figures. It is also worth asking which body supervises the practice for anti-money-laundering purposes and whether they hold professional indemnity insurance.

extra_faqs.q: Do I need to bring anything to a first appointment?
extra_faqs.a: A list of your properties, how each is held and any lender requests you have received will give the accountant a useful starting point. If you already track income and spending, bring a sample so they can see how your records are kept and where help is needed.
